Other Selected Cooling System Projects Livermore continues to push the boundaries of computer system cooling through various other collaborations and projects on going and completed. Cutting edge immersion cooling LLNL is collaborating with Sandia Laboratories to push forward the research in computer cooling systems. There are current collaborations involving emersion cooling projects. Emersion cooling involves submerging electrical systems in non-conductive liquids to more efficiently capture the heat produced [23]. There are estimates that this could cut energy consumptions for data centers by 70%. Non liquid cooling systems for high powered electrical devices Non liquid cooling of high-powered devices is not new to LLNL. LLNL holds patents around cooling high power devices without the use of liquids. The novel approach presented in the US patent entitled, “Systems and methods for cooling high power devices” uses a thermoelectric cooler (TEC) embedded electronics system [24]. The system uses TEC material as an active cooling element. The configuration of TEC allows heat to dissipate, cooling the electrical components without the use of fluids [25]. This novel process is compatible with the thin film TEC material and standard integrated circuitry. This was originally developed for laser diodes but has broad applications and poses possibilities for further high energy system cooling. Next generation network and optophotonics advancement Data Center Market Report – LLNL-TR-2013901 9 In 2022, LLNL began collaborating with Sandia National Laboratories, Los Alamos National Laboratory, and Cornelis Networks to develop the next generation of interconnect technologies for high performance computing. The collaboration was focused on accelerating the development of network simulations to overcome InfiniBand era limits and meet exascale, AI/ML, data center demands [26]. Livermore has also been involved with the development of more efficient optical cables for meaningful energy savings relating to data transmission. In 2024, LLNL received continued funding for a collaboration with Flawless Photonics. This collaboration involves Livermore researchers simulating and modeling defects in fiber optic manufacturing with the goal of achieving highly efficient optical cable production [27]. Conclusions The data center market is poised to boom due to the rapid adoption of AI and continued adoption of high compute systems across enterprises [1]. There are opportunities for innovation in this market as capital expenditure investment increases to meet the rising demand. Two key areas of interest for data center market growth are new site identification and increased compute power. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory is uniquely positioned with expertise to help mitigate risks associated with these areas.
